4. The petitioner filed an application on 12-10-2015 under Order VII, rule-11 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain to reject the plaint or in the alternative to return the plaint under Order VII, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57, Artha Rin Adalat Ain. The same day the respondent No. 3 the plaintiff Bank filed a separate application for extension of the order of attachment and the Court fixed the next date for 10-11-2015 for filing of written objection of the plaintiff Bank, against the application dated 12-10-2015 and for hearing the same. The plaintiff bank on 10-11-2015, filed a separate application praying for extension of the Order of attachment before judgment and another application under section 13(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain to pass judgment and decree as per admission of petitioner. The court disallowed the application of the defendant No. 3 petitioner filed under Order VII, rule 11 for rejection of the plaint or in the alternative to return the plaint under Order VI, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure on contest, and allowed the petition for extension of the period of attachment filed by Bank till 5-1-2016. 

 10. From a plain reading of this provision it is apparent that the affidavit under section 6(2) must be in a manner which is declaratory of conversance with and in attestation of the documents submitted in court in support of the claim of the plaintiff. In the event the suit is disposed of ex-parte, the absence of this declaration as regards the veracity of the documents becomes relevant and any ex-parte decree if passed in suit in the basis of the same affidavit without examination of witness and formal proof of documents would be inadequate and liable to be set-aside.
